lessons.lessonTitle: Recognizing Shared Cyrillic Consonants: М, Т, К, О, А
lessons.primaryPurpose: Introduce printed capital and lowercase letterforms for shared Cyrillic consonants and cardinal anchor vowels.
lessons.communicativeOutcome: Visually identify and match Cyrillic letters М, Т, К, О, and А against identical Latin and international glyphs.

exercises.exerciseTitle: Recognizing Shared Cyrillic Capital 'М'

options.explanation: Correct! Cyrillic 'М' represents /m/ and shares its glyph form with Latin 'M'.

options.text: И
options.explanation: Incorrect. 'И' represents the vowel /i/, which looks like a reversed 'N'.

options.text: П
options.explanation: Incorrect. 'П' represents the voiceless stop /p/ (Greek Pi).

options.text: Л
options.explanation: Incorrect. 'Л' represents the lateral liquid /l/.

exercises.correctAnswer: М
exercises.explanation: Cyrillic uppercase 'М' and lowercase 'м' represent the voiced bilabial nasal consonant /m/. It is visually identical to Latin 'M'.

lessons.primaryPurpose: Train the ear to differentiate the open mid-rounded back vowel /ɔ/ from the front-rounded /ɵ/, and /ʊ/ from /u/.
lessons.communicativeOutcome: Accurately discern minimal pairs such as ор (bed/place) vs өр (debt), and ус (water) vs үс (hair).

exercises.exerciseTitle: Detecting Harmonic Violations in Nonce Words
exercises.prompt: Which of the following hypothetical word roots VIOLATES Mongolian vowel harmony rules by mixing masculine and feminine vowels?
exercises.hint: A single native root cannot contain both 'а' (masculine) and 'э' (feminine).

options.text: *мадэ (contains masculine 'а' and feminine 'э')
options.explanation: Correct! Mixing back 'а' with front 'э' in a single stem is strictly prohibited by vowel harmony.

options.text: малгай (all back vowels: а, а, ай)
options.explanation: Incorrect. 'малгай' is fully harmonic (masculine).

options.text: нөхөр (all front rounded vowels: ө)
options.explanation: Incorrect. 'нөхөр' is fully harmonic (feminine).

options.text: охин (neutral 'и' with back 'о')
options.explanation: Incorrect. The neutral vowel 'и' can freely occur with back vowels.

exercises.correctAnswer: *мадэ (contains masculine 'а' and feminine 'э')
exercises.explanation: Native Mongolian roots maintain strict vowel harmony: back vowels (а, о, у) never co-occur with front vowels (э, ө, ү). Therefore, '*мадэ' is impossible.

learnerFeedback.onSuccess: Яг зөв! '*мадэ' illegally mixes back 'а' and front 'э'.
learnerFeedback.onFailure: Remember: Masculine and feminine vowels can never mix in a native root.

exercises.detailedGrammarNote: The only exception to pure harmonic separation is the neutral vowel 'и', which may appear in both masculine and feminine words without changing the dominant gender of the root.

lessons.lessonTitle: The Architecture of Mongolian Sentences: Head-Final SOV Word Order
lessons.primaryPurpose: Introduce the canonical Subject-Object-Verb (SOV) sentence topology of Modern Mongolian.
lessons.communicativeOutcome: Recognize that modifiers precede heads and the finite predicate anchors the absolute end of the clause.

exercises.exerciseTitle: Assembling Canonical SOV Word Order
exercises.prompt: Arrange the scrambled word tokens into a grammatically correct Mongolian declarative sentence: 'I will read a book'.
exercises.correctAnswer: би ном уншина
exercises.hint: In Mongolian, the subject comes first, the direct object comes second, and the verb always stands at the end.
exercises.explanation: Mongolian is strictly head-final with canonical Subject-Object-Verb (SOV) order. 'Би' (Subject) precedes 'ном' (Object), and 'уншина' (Verb) must terminate the clause.

learnerFeedback.onSuccess: Маш сайн! You placed the verb at the clause-final anchor.
learnerFeedback.onFailure: Remember: Subject (Би) + Object (ном) + Verb (уншина).

exercises.detailedGrammarNote: Modern Mongolian strictly prohibits English-style SVO ordering (*Би уншина ном). The finite predicate holds the absolute right edge of the sentence.

options.explanation: Incorrect. This is a postpositional locative phrase.

exercises.correctAnswer: ирнэ (will come) - Clause-final verb
exercises.explanation: The finite verb 'ирнэ' (comes/will come) concludes the clause, serving as the syntactic head to which all preceding arguments link.

learnerFeedback.onFailure: The predicate in Mongolian is the verb at the very end: 'ирнэ'.

exercises.detailedGrammarNote: Because Mongolian is head-final, modifiers (temporal, locative, direct objects) always precede the verb head, and attributive adjectives precede the noun head.

lessons.lessonTitle: Abstract Nouns in the Workplace: Nominalizers -дал/-дэл and -лга/-лгэ

learnerFeedback.onFailure: 'хариуц-' + '-лага' = 'хариуцлага'.

exercises.detailedGrammarNote: The productive deverbal nominalizer suffix -лга⁴ (-лага, -лэг, -лого, -лөгөө) transforms action verbs into institutional abstract concepts, processes, and corporate obligations.

options.text: байшил
options.explanation: Incorrect. Non-existent derivation.

exercises.correctAnswer: байдал (situation / state / condition)

exercises.prompt: In academic and political Mongolian, what is the precise syntactic and pragmatic difference between the discourse particles 'бол' and 'харин'?
exercises.hint: 'Бол' introduces or grounds the theme; 'харин' pivots to introduce a sharp contrasting argument.

options.text: 'Бол' marks the established topic / baseline theme (As for X...); 'харин' introduces a contrastive topic or adversative shift (Whereas Y / On the other hand, Y...).
options.cyrillic: бол бол сэдэв заах, харин бол эсрэгцүүлэн тодотгох
options.explanation: Correct! 'Бол' establishes the frame of reference; 'харин' introduces the contrasting counterpart.

options.text: 'Бол' is only used in colloquial slang, while 'харин' is only used in ancient poetry.
options.explanation: Incorrect. Both are vital across all modern registers.

options.text: 'Бол' is a past tense suffix, while 'харин' is a question particle.
options.explanation: Incorrect. Neither is a verbal tense suffix.

exercises.correctAnswer: 'Бол' marks the established topic / baseline theme (As for X...); 'харин' introduces a contrastive topic or adversative shift (Whereas Y / On the other hand, Y...).
acceptableAlternatives: бол marks topic, харин marks contrastive topic
exercises.explanation: 'Бол' marks the topical ground of a proposition, while 'харин' serves as a contrastive discourse marker setting up an antithetical balance.

learnerFeedback.onSuccess: Маш сайн! Masterful grasp of Mongolian information packaging.
learnerFeedback.onFailure: 'Бол' establishes the theme; 'харин' creates the contrast.

exercises.prompt:
An editor found this flawed line in an agrarian policy article:

'*Харин газар тариалангийн салбар гантай байсан, бол мал аж ахуйн салбар өсөлттэй гарлаа.'

exercises.exerciseTitle: Constitutional Statutory Parsing: Article 16 Fundamental Rights

'Монгол Улсын иргэн дараах үндсэн эрх, эрх чөлөөг баталгаатай эдэлнэ:
1/ Амьд явах эрхтэй. Монгол Улсын Эрүүгийн хуульд заасан онц хүнд гэмт хэрэг үйлдсэний учир шүүхийн хүчин төгөлдөр тогтоолоор ялын дээд хэмжээ оногдуулснаас бусад тохиолдолд хүний амь нас бусниулахыг хатуу хориглоно.'

What is the strict constitutional threshold established for limiting the fundamental right to life?

exercises.hint: Note the strict procedural requirement: only upon a valid court judgment for extraordinarily grave crimes defined specifically in the Criminal Code.

options.text: It can strictly only occur upon a legally in-force final court judgment for exceptionally grave crimes explicitly prescribed in the Criminal Code; in all other instances, deprivation of life is strictly prohibited.
options.cyrillic: Шүүхийн хүчин төгөлдөр тогтоолоос бусад тохиолдолд хатуу хориглох
options.explanation: Correct! The constitutional text permits limitation only under in-force judicial sentence for statutorily defined grave crimes.

options.text: The Prime Minister or police can suspend the right to life during economic downturns.
options.explanation: Incorrect. The executive branch has zero power to alter this right.

options.text: The text states the right to life cannot be regulated by any court under any circumstance.
options.explanation: Incorrect. The text contains the historical proviso regarding judicial sentencing.

exercises.correctAnswer: It can strictly only occur upon a legally in-force final court judgment for exceptionally grave crimes explicitly prescribed in the Criminal Code; in all other instances, deprivation of life is strictly prohibited.

options.text: Regressive place assimilation: Word-final coronal /n/ assimilates to the place of articulation of the adjacent consonant (e.g. becoming bilabial [m] before /b, p, m/, and velar [ŋ] in pause or before velars).

options.text: Progressive devoicing: The following initial voiced plosive (/b/ or /g/) is completely devoiced and aspirated by the preceding coronal nasal.
options.explanation: Incorrect. Mongolian nasals are voiced sonorants and trigger regressive place assimilation, not progressive devoicing.

options.text: Complete nasal deletion without compensatory vowel nasalization, leaving an open syllable.
options.explanation: Incorrect. The coronal nasal does not delete across boundaries; it assimilates to the place of the succeeding consonant.

exercises.explanation: Coronal /n/ assimilates to bilabial [m] before labials (e.g. 'арван бууз' -> [арвам бууз]) and velar [ŋ] before velars ('арван гэр' -> [арваҥ гэр]).
